notes.title: Start here: the architectural-cartographer guides for Umami
notes.body:
Umami is an open-source, privacy-focused web analytics app on the Next.js App Router. This quest uses `umami/docs/architectural-cartographer/`, a three-level track:

1. `01-junior-engineer.md`: setup, folder orientation, three React component anatomies (MetricCard, WebsiteChart, WebsiteAddForm) and three backend route anatomies.
2. `02-mid-level-engineer.md`: architecture diagram, state management, the API contract map, a full trace of the pageviews chart, non-obvious patterns.
3. `03-senior-engineer.md`: findings and a map of the main seams.

`00-reading-map.md` lists the files in a sensible reading order.

The guides quote shortened code with comments. Every quiz in this quest is about what the real file does for a specific input, so open each cited file under `umami/src/` and read the complete function. Pay attention to types at the boundary (what Zod actually produces), to defaults, and to which branch runs first.

excerpts.quote: Server data lives in TanStack Query.

readMore.why: The suggested reading order through the Umami codebase.

notes.title: Concept: client data fetching and derived numbers
notes.body:
**React Query defaults.** `src/app/Providers.tsx` creates one `QueryClient` for the whole app with `defaultOptions.queries`. Look up what each of the three options means in the TanStack Query docs (retries after an error, refetching when the window regains focus, and how long fetched data counts as fresh), then read the values Umami sets.

**The API client.** `src/components/hooks/useApi.ts` builds every request. Read `getUrl` and work out the URL for a relative path with and without a configured base path. Then read how `defaultHeaders` is assembled and under which condition share headers are added.

**Derived numbers in a component.** `MetricCard` receives a current `value` and a `change` and derives a percentage. Work the formula by hand for a few inputs, including one where the previous period was zero. The guide's journal notes the prop is easy to misuse; decide for yourself what `change` means.

readMore.why: The app-wide providers, including the QueryClient.

notes.title: Concept: website routes and pluggable storage
notes.body:
**Website routes.** `src/app/api/websites/route.ts` has a GET (list) and a POST (create). For GET, look closely at how the `includeTeams` parameter is declared in the Zod schema and how the route tests it. For POST, list in order: the CLOUD_MODE branch, the permission checks, how the `data` object is built (which owner fields depend on `teamId`), and what happens with `shareId`.

**Read routes.** `src/app/api/websites/[websiteId]/pageviews/route.ts` is the template for analytics reads: parse, authorize, build filters, query. Note which response helper it uses when authorization fails.

**Storage dispatch.** Analytics queries pass an object of implementations to `runQuery` in `src/lib/db.ts`. Read `getDatabaseType` and `runQuery` together and write down, for each combination of `CLICKHOUSE_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`, which implementation is called.

notes.title: Why a denied pageviews read is a 401
notes.body:
After `parseRequest` succeeds, the route awaits the `websiteId` param and checks `canViewWebsite(auth, websiteId)`. When that is false it returns `unauthorized()`, which is a 401 response, even though the user is signed in. Umami's read routes use unauthorized() for both "not signed in" and "not allowed".

- *403 forbidden()*: this route does not call forbidden().
- *404*: the route does not hide the id behind a 404.
- *200 with empty arrays*: the queries never run.

notes.title: Why a failed query is not retried
notes.body:
`Providers.tsx` builds the QueryClient with `retry: false`. TanStack Query's own default is to retry a failed query three times with backoff; Umami turns that off globally, so the error state appears after the first failure.

- *3 retries*: that is the library default, overridden here.
- *Retry after the stale time*: staleTime controls freshness, not retries.
- *Retry on focus*: refetchOnWindowFocus is also false.

notes.title: Why returning to the tab does not refetch
notes.body:
The QueryClient sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. After five minutes the data is stale (staleTime is one minute), but stale data is only refetched by a trigger, and window focus is no longer one. A refetch happens on the next mount of a component using the query, or on an explicit invalidation.

- *Refetch because stale*: staleness alone does not trigger a fetch.
- *Refetch every query*: no focus refetch happens at all.
- *Clear and reload*: React Query never reloads the page.

notes.title: How MetricCard turns a delta into a percent
notes.body:
`change` is the delta, so the component recovers the previous value as `diff = value - change` = 100. Then `pct = ((value - diff) / diff) * 100` = 20 / 100 * 100 = 20. The percent is relative to the previous period, as a growth figure should be.

- *16.7%*: that divides the delta by the current value instead of the previous one.
- *120%*: no step divides the value by the change.
- *-20%*: the delta is positive, so the result is positive.

excerpts.quote: const pct = diff !== 0 ? ((value - diff) / diff) * 100 : value !== 0 ? 100 : 0;

notes.title: What MetricCard shows when the base is zero
notes.body:
With value 50 and change 50, `diff` is 0. The ternary checks `diff !== 0` first, so no division happens; then `value !== 0` is true and pct is 100. Only value 0 with diff 0 gives 0.

- *Infinity*: the division is skipped exactly to avoid this.
- *0 whenever the previous value is zero*: 0 needs the current value to be zero too.
- *NaN*: no 0/0 division ever runs.

notes.title: Why includeTeams=false still includes teams
notes.body:
The schema declares `includeTeams: z.string().optional()`, so the parsed value is the string "false". The route tests `if (query.includeTeams)`, and every non-empty string is truthy in JavaScript, so it returns `getAllUserWebsitesIncludingTeamOwner`. To get only personal websites, the parameter has to be left out.

- *Only own websites*: that branch runs only when the parameter is absent or empty.
- *400*: a string is exactly what the schema expects.
- *Only team websites*: no branch returns team websites alone.

notes.title: Who owns a website created in a team
notes.body:
The route builds `data` with `id`, `createdBy: auth.user.id`, `name`, `domain` and `teamId`, and adds `data.userId = auth.user.id` only `if (!teamId)`. A team website therefore has teamId and createdBy but no userId, which is how canViewWebsite knows to check team membership.

- *userId set, teamId dropped*: teamId is always copied into data.
- *All three*: userId is skipped when teamId is present.
- *Team only, no creator*: createdBy is always recorded.

notes.title: What shareId does at creation time
notes.body:
After `createWebsite`, the route calls `createShare` when `shareId` is present: a new share with `entityId` set to the website, `shareType` website, the website name, `slug: shareId`, and overview and events parameters. The response includes `shareId` taken from the share's slug.

- *A column on the website*: the slug lives on the share row.
- *Ignored*: the share is created in the same request.
- *A public flag*: visibility is expressed by the share, not by a flag.

notes.title: Why the cloud website limit answers 401
notes.body:
In CLOUD_MODE and without a teamId, the route fetches the account. If it has no subscription and the user's website count is at `CLOUD_WEBSITE_LIMIT`, it returns `unauthorized({ message: 'Website limit reached.' })`, a 401. This branch runs before the permission checks.

- *402*: the route has no 402 response.
- *403 from canCreateWebsite*: a failed permission check also uses unauthorized(), and it runs later.
- *Created disabled*: nothing is created.

notes.title: Which implementation runQuery picks first
notes.body:
`runQuery` checks `process.env.CLICKHOUSE_URL` first. Inside that branch it returns `queries[KAFKA]()` if the object has a kafka entry, else `queries[CLICKHOUSE]()`. The Prisma entry is used only when CLICKHOUSE_URL is unset and the database type is postgresql.

- *ClickHouse*: used under ClickHouse only when no kafka entry is given.
- *Prisma because DATABASE_URL is set*: the ClickHouse branch returns before the database type is examined.
- *Both*: each branch returns a single call.

notes.title: What runQuery does for a MySQL URL
notes.body:
`getDatabaseType` takes the URL scheme, maps `postgres` to `postgresql`, and returns anything else unchanged, here "mysql". `runQuery` then only has `if (db === POSTGRESQL)`; there is no else branch, so the function ends and returns undefined. Nothing throws.

- *Prisma for every SQL URL*: the code calls Prisma only for postgresql.
- *notImplemented()*: that helper exists in the file but runQuery does not call it.
- *ClickHouse by default*: ClickHouse needs CLICKHOUSE_URL.

notes.title: How useApi builds request URLs
notes.body:
`getUrl` returns absolute `http` URLs unchanged; for anything else it returns `basePath || ''`, then `/api`, then the given path. With basePath "/analytics" the request goes to /analytics/api/websites/w1/pageviews.

- */api first, base path ignored*: the base path is prepended when set.
- *No /api segment*: /api is always inserted for relative paths.
- *Absolute https URL*: only an http-prefixed input stays absolute; nothing builds one from the hostname.

notes.title: When useApi sends share headers
notes.body:
`shareHeaders` is filled only when `isSharePath && shareToken?.token`, and `isSharePath` is true only for pathnames that start with /share. On /websites/w1 the share headers stay empty. `defaultHeaders` always contains `authorization: Bearer <client token>`, so the request carries the bearer header alone.

- *Both share headers too*: the path condition fails.
- *Share token only*: the bearer header is always included.
- *No headers*: the client stores its token itself and sends it as a bearer header; it does not rely on a cookie.
